title: fix(metadata-protocol): a widget probe refused by read admission names the caller's read access, not a dataset edit
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuDWJsBGQpadCH8JR2xZQ5re)_

Fixes #25544

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What was wrong

`POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts` probes each dashboard widget by running `queryDataset` as the publishing caller. A publisher who may not read the dataset's object gets an error-tier `widget_query_failed` issue. Its message is right (`[Analytics] Access denied: reading "task_item" is not permitted for this user.`). Its `fix` was not: the widget plane's `catch` gave one fix for every throw, "Fix the dataset definition (or the widget's values/dimensions) so the query compiles, then republish." The dataset was correct. An author or agent who followed the fix would edit a working dataset.

## What changed

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts`, the widget plane's `catch` only:

- **The discriminator is the error's ADR-0112 `code`, not its message.** The analytics service's read admission throws `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `status: 403`, `object: OBJECT_NAME` (`read-admission.ts`), and the field-level gate throws the same code with `fields` (`field-read-admission.ts`). `readAdmissionRefusal(e)` matches on `code === PERMISSION_DENIED` (typed as `StandardErrorCode`) and reads `object` and `fields` from the error.
- **An access refusal gets an access fix.** The fix says dataset `DATASET_NAME` is not the cause and needs no change, that the publisher (or the role the dashboard is for) needs read access to the refused object (and the refused fields when the error names them), and that the finding is about this caller: a viewer who has that access can read the widget. The object comes from the error first, because a joined object can be the one refused. The dataset's `object` is the fallback.
- **One `PERMISSION_DENIED` stays on the dataset fix.** `fieldReadUnjudgeableError` (a member that is not a column reference) carries `member`, and its remedy is a dataset change. A `member` on the error therefore keeps the old fix.
- **Unchanged:** `code` (`widget_query_failed`), `severity` (`error`), `message`, and every other probe plane.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes-widget-refusal-fix.test.ts` (new) runs `runBuildProbes` with errors built the way the analytics service builds them. Six cases: object refusal → access fix; joined-object refusal → names the joined object; field refusal → names the fields; `DATASET_INVALID` → dataset fix; `PERMISSION_DENIED` with `member` → dataset fix; bare `Error` → dataset fix. Each case also checks that `code`, `severity`, `ref` and `message` did not change.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-publish-drafts-probe-caller-context.test.ts` exercises the real path: the door, `publishPackageDrafts`, `runBuildProbes` and a real `AnalyticsService`. The non-reader case now checks that the fix names `read access to object "task_item"` and is not the dataset fix. A new third case publishes, as the reader, a dataset whose measure reads a relationship path missing from `include`. The real compiler refuses it (`DATASET_INVALID`), and the dataset fix is kept.

**Ablation, run once (runtime imports `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` through `dist/`, so it was rebuilt):** `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` changed `err.code !== PERMISSION_DENIED` to `err.code !== 'ABLATION_25544'`. Its output: `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob b4e89c9068d6 -> 2de0ef3cb9ab`. After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol build`, `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` printed `✓ dist/: marker present in 2 built files`. The tsup JS emitted; the dts step exited 1 because the now-unused constant tripped `noUnusedLocals`, and the JS is what the suites import.
- Unit file: `3 failed | 3 passed (6)`. The three access arms went red; the three dataset-fix arms stayed green.
- Runtime pin: `1 failed | 2 passed (3)`. The non-reader case went red.

Restore: `ok restored: blob == HEAD (b4e89c9068d6) and git diff HEAD is empty`. After a rebuild, the preflight with `--absent` printed `✓ dist/: marker absent from all 24 built files`. Both suites were green again: `6 passed (6)` and `3 passed (3)`.

## Local verification

All readings on the final head `967be5c033`.

- **Build closure (①):** `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' --filter '@objectstack/metadata-protocol' build` under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` — `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **Affected packages (②):** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` — `Test Files 263 passed | 3 skipped (266)`, `Tests 21466 passed | 19 skipped (21485)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` — `Test Files 440 passed (440)`, `Tests 7035 passed | 19 skipped (7054)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` — both exit 0, in the same locked `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **Derived families (③):** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 69 commands; every one was run with its exit code captured before any pipe. All 69 exited 0. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran ran.list --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` → `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 69 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 69 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`.
  - Two of the 69 were red on an earlier head and are green here: `pnpm check:error-code-casing` (exit 1 — the new test's `'widget_query_failed'` literal needed the ADR-0112 D6c `adr0112-ok:` reason the sibling pin already carries; added, now `✓ no unlisted lowercase error codes in 9427 scanned file(s)`) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3 — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, 38 packages had no `dist/` in this worktree; green once the closure was built).
- **Repo scan:** `pnpm lint` — exit 0.
- **NOT MEASURED:** the 52 artifact-roster families, the 10 declared wide-population families, the 5 path-scheduled CI jobs (`Test Core`, `Build Core`, and the three `main`-only batteries), the 4 CI type-check lanes and the always-runs tail — each outside the derived set and owned by CI, per the tool's own accounting. `pnpm check:dev-prereqs` and `pnpm check:skill-frame-freshness`: not derived and not owed (no `packages/spec` build and no four-axis frame file in the diff).
- **Dogfood battery:** n/a — no `!` in the title and `Clause-②: no` carries no `(narrowing)` arm.

## Acceptance notes

- The analytics service gives three different `PERMISSION_DENIED` refusals the same structured shape: `code`, `status` and `object` and nothing else. They are the object read-admission denial (`readAdmissionDeniedError`), "the field-level read permissions could not be resolved" (`fieldReadUnresolvedError`) and "the API exposure declaration could not be resolved" (`exposureUnresolvedError`). A consumer cannot tell "the caller has no grant" from "the gate could not reach a verdict" without reading the prose. This PR does not read the prose. The two unresolved cases therefore get the access fix, which is right about the dataset ("not the cause") and only partly right about the remedy (an operator fault, not a missing grant). A stable discriminator such as a `reason` field belongs to `packages/services/service-analytics`. That is the services seat's surface and is not edited here.
